chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa’eed, from Jameel, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, Allah’s blessings be upon them both, that he said: I said to him: A man who bequeaths with something of his property?
Then he said to me: (It is mentioned) In the Book of Ali, peace be upon him: Something of his property is (equivalent to) one of six.

key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: the Book of Ali (referring to a specific legal text or compilation attributed to Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'something' (shay') mean in Islamic inheritance and bequest law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) clarifies the legal definition of 'something' (shay') in bequests, specifying it as one of six fractional shares, a ruling derived from the legal codification in the *Musannaf* of Imam Ali. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise quantification in inheritance law to prevent ambiguity in testamentary dispositions.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammed bin Ahmad, from Ali bin Sindi, from Muhammed bin Amru bin Sa’eed, from Jameel, from Aban bin Taghlib, from Abu Hamza, from Ali bin Hussain, Allah’s blessings be upon them both, that he said: I said to him: A man who bequeaths with something of his property?
Then he said to me: (It is mentioned) In the Book of Ali, peace be upon him: Something of his property is (equivalent to) one of six.
